sentences.en: G'day, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余味》（The Rest is History）。

sentences.en: The history of Australia is littered with marvels and wonders, from the sporting high points of the 1981 Ashes and the 2003 Rugby Union World Cup
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的历史充满了奇迹与惊叹，从1981年灰烬杯板球赛和2003年橄榄球世界杯的体育高光时刻，

sentences.en: Final, to high culture, the career of Paul Hogan, or the music of Midnight Oil.
sentences.zh: 到高雅文化、保罗·霍根的职业生涯，或是“午夜油”乐队的音乐。

sentences.en: But Tom, if we were picking one point where Australian history really started, could you do better than
sentences.zh: 但是汤姆，如果我们非要选一个澳大利亚历史真正开始的时间点，你觉得还有比

sentences.en: the statue in Hyde Park, Sydney, of Captain Cook that bears the inscription, Discovered This Territory,
sentences.zh: 悉尼海德公园里那座库克船长雕像更好的选择吗？雕像上刻着：“1770年发现此地”。

sentences.en: What do you think of that?
sentences.zh: 你对此怎么看？

sentences.en: I think you've just given the most pommy introduction to Australian history imaginable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你刚才给出的这段澳大利亚历史介绍，简直是再“英国佬”不过了。

sentences.en: And if there are any Australian listeners left after that introduction, they won't be running for the outback.
sentences.zh: 如果听完这段介绍还有澳大利亚听众没走，那他们肯定不是往内陆跑了。

sentences.en: Yes, well,
sentences.zh: 是啊，好吧，

sentences.en: we do have quite a lot of Australian listeners, and we've had quite a lot of Australian listeners saying, are we going to do something on the history of Australia?
sentences.zh: 我们确实有很多澳大利亚听众，也有很多听众问我们，什么时候能讲讲澳大利亚的历史？

sentences.en: They surely would have known we'd start with an introduction like that.
sentences.zh: 他们肯定早就料到我们会用那样的开场白。

sentences.en: I'm sure they did.
sentences.zh: 我相信他们料到了。

sentences.en: I'm sure that's what they wanted.
sentences.zh: 我相信这正是他们想要的。

sentences.en: And I said, well, who should we get on?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我们该请谁来呢？

sentences.en: And the universal consensus of Australia was that we should get on our guest today, who is David Hunt, who has written three histories of Australia, all of them with the name,
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚各界一致认为，我们应该请今天的嘉宾大卫·亨特。他写过三本澳大利亚历史书，书名里都带有一个词，

sentences.en: the word Gert in, as in Gert with, you know, a moat or whatever.
sentences.zh: 就是“Gert”，就像“Gert with”那种，你知道，护城河之类的词。

sentences.en: So Gert, the unauthorised history of Australia, True Gert and Gert Nation.
sentences.zh: 所以书名分别是《Gert：澳大利亚非官方历史》、《真正的Gert》和《Gert国度》。

sentences.en: He's also a broadcaster who's made a film for
sentences.zh: 他也是一位广播员，曾为历史频道制作过一部纪录片，

sentences.en: History Channel called Aussie Inventions That Changed the World.
sentences.zh: 名叫《改变世界的澳大利亚发明》。

sentences.en: And he's a podcaster, award-winning podcaster of Rum, Rebels and Ratbags, which I think, David, the logo of that is, is that Captain Cook?
sentences.zh: 他还是播客《朗姆酒、反叛者与流氓》（Rum, Rebels and Ratbags）的主播，这档节目还获了奖。大卫，我想问一下，那个节目的标志是库克船长吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 正是。

sentences.en: It's, it's, it's Captain Cook wearing a silly British hat, which is...
sentences.zh: 那是……那是戴着一顶滑稽英国帽子的库克船长，这简直是……

sentences.en: There's no such thing.
sentences.zh: 根本没那回事。

sentences.en: There's no such thing, David.
sentences.zh: 根本没那回事，大卫。

sentences.en: I don't know what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: British hats are always sensible.
sentences.zh: 英国帽子向来都很得体。

sentences.en: I'm very disappointed that you did not mention the T20 2021 victory the other day as part of the great Australian sporting history.
sentences.zh: 我很失望，你刚才竟然没把前几天的2021年T20板球赛胜利列入伟大的澳大利亚体育史。

sentences.en: I've no idea what you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道你在说什么。

sentences.en: And everyone knows that 2020 is a ludicrous format and the test, it's the ashes that matter.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道T20是一种荒谬的赛制，测试赛，也就是灰烬杯，那才是最重要的。

sentences.en: So, David.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Captain Cook, great hero in Australia, but until recently, when it's slightly changed, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 库克船长，澳大利亚的伟大英雄，但直到最近，情况稍微有点变化了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, look, when I went to school and I'm, I'm going to date myself here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，我上学的时候——我这可是暴露年龄了。

sentences.en: I remember Dennis
sentences.zh: 我记得丹尼斯·利利（Dennis Lillee）

sentences.en: Lilly playing vaguely as a young fella.
sentences.zh: 打球时我还是个小伙子。

sentences.en: So I've just hit 50.
sentences.zh: 所以我刚满50岁。

sentences.en: When I went to school in the 1970s and 1980s, we were effectively taught as students that Captain Cook discovered Australia.
sentences.zh: 我在上世纪七八十年代上学时，学校实际上教导我们说库克船长发现了澳大利亚。

sentences.en: And that was the conventional wisdom and the school curricula had a very British view of Australian history.
sentences.zh: 那是当时的共识，学校课程对澳大利亚历史有着非常英国化的视角。

sentences.en: Recently, the Australian history curriculum has been far more complex and far more nuanced.
sentences.zh: 最近，澳大利亚的历史课程变得复杂得多，也微妙得多。

sentences.en: And there is an upwelling of criticism about statues of our colonial figures.
sentences.zh: 而且对于我们殖民时期人物雕像的批评声也日益高涨。

sentences.en: We have to import debates from other countries before we actually have them here.
sentences.zh: 我们总是先从其他国家引入辩论，然后才在本地展开讨论。

sentences.en: So we have to see Americans and Brits getting angry about statues before we do the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得先看到美国人和英国人对雕像感到愤怒，我们才会做同样的事。

sentences.en: But the statue of Captain Cook in Hyde Park has discovered this territory 1770,
sentences.zh: 但海德公园里那座库克船长的雕像上写着“1770年发现此地”，

sentences.en: which is regarded as an insult to the Indigenous people who discovered this territory some 65,000 years ago,
sentences.zh: 这被视为对原住民的侮辱，因为他们早在约65000年前就发现了这片土地，

sentences.en: give or take a few millennia, and all of the various other people who landed on these fair shores pre-Cook, who wasn't even Captain Cook at the time.
sentences.zh: 误差不过几千年，还有其他各种在库克之前就登上这片美丽海岸的人，当时他甚至还不是库克船长。

sentences.en: He was a lieutenant.
sentences.zh: 他当时只是个中尉。

sentences.en: The British perspective, I mean, we were always taught, if we were taught about Australia at all,
sentences.zh: 英国人的视角，我是说，我们如果学过澳大利亚历史的话，

sentences.en: or if it was a sort of, you know, a page about Australia in a kind of world history textbook, it always was, you know, Captain Cook discovered...
sentences.zh: 或者如果世界历史教科书里有关于澳大利亚的一页，总是写着，你知道，库克船长发现了……

sentences.en: There was a Lady Bird book, wasn't there?
sentences.zh: 有一本“瓢虫书”（Ladybird book），对吧？

sentences.en: There was a Lady Bird book of Captain Cook.
sentences.zh: 有一本关于库克船长的“瓢虫书”。

sentences.en: There was a Lady Bird, but that was exactly...
sentences.zh: 确实有，但那正是……

sentences.en: So that's the measure of fame in English history.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国历史中衡量名气的标准。

sentences.en: A great canonical...
sentences.zh: 一部伟大的经典……

sentences.en: Can you join and discover Australia?
sentences.zh: 你能加入并发现澳大利亚吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: That's exactly it.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so Captain Cook is, you know, just give us a little portrait of him.
sentences.zh: 所以库克船长，给我们简单描绘一下他吧。

sentences.en: Because he's not a kind of terrible guy, is he?
sentences.zh: 因为他不是那种十恶不赦的人，对吧？

sentences.en: Like a conquistador or something?
sentences.zh: 不像征服者之类的？

sentences.en: I mean, he's a kind of admirable figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他算是一个令人钦佩的人物。

sentences.en: He's a kind of great navigator.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的航海家。

sentences.en: Undisputedly a great navigator.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问是一位伟大的航海家。

sentences.en: I mean, when he was picked for the Endeavour expedition to Australia, he was actually a fairly lowly warrant officer who'd served over in the Seven Years' War,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当他被选中参加“奋进号”澳大利亚探险时，他实际上只是一个地位相当低微的准尉，曾在七年战争中服役，

sentences.en: posted to Canada, killed a few Frenchmen, which was regarded as good sport,
sentences.zh: 被派往加拿大，杀了一些法国人，这在当时被视为一种不错的消遣，

sentences.en: but was noted for his cartography and also noted for writing a learned paper on the sun and navigation.
sentences.zh: 但他因制图技术而闻名，也因撰写了一篇关于太阳和航海的学术论文而受到关注。

sentences.en: Because he was basically self-taught, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上是自学成才的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he was from very humble stock.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他出身非常卑微。

sentences.en: He was kind of father as a farm labourer and...
sentences.zh: 他父亲是个农场工人，然后……

sentences.en: Yeah, he was a grocer's apprentice and took to sailing fairly late in life, serving on the free love, a sort of bohemian coal-carrying vessel that plied the channel,
sentences.zh: 是的，他曾是杂货店学徒，很晚才开始航海，在“自由号”上服役，那是一种往返于海峡的波西米亚风格运煤船，

sentences.en: and finds himself over in Canada.
sentences.zh: 后来他发现自己到了加拿大。

sentences.en: But look, undisputably a great navigator, but he was chosen for the Endeavour voyage because the primary purpose of it was to measure the transit of Venus across the sun in 1869...
sentences.zh: 但听着，他毫无疑问是一位伟大的航海家，但他被选中参加“奋进号”航行，是因为其主要目的是测量1769年金星凌日……

sentences.en: Sorry, 1769 in Tahiti.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，是1769年在塔希提岛。

sentences.en: And so, because he was a good cartographer, because he was an experienced amateur astronomer,
sentences.zh: 所以，因为他是一位出色的制图师，因为他是一位经验丰富的业余天文学家，

sentences.en: the Royal Society promotes him effectively, or the Admiralty promotes him from warrant officer to lieutenant,
sentences.zh: 皇家学会实际上提拔了他，或者说海军部将他从准尉提拔为中尉，

sentences.en: and posts him off to the other side of the world to measure this astronomical phenomena, to help measure longitude more effectively.
sentences.zh: 并把他派往地球的另一端去测量这一天文现象，以帮助更有效地测量经度。

sentences.en: They thought that if we can make this precise calculation of how long it takes Venus to track across the face of the sun,
sentences.zh: 他们认为，如果我们能精确计算出金星穿过太阳表面所需的时间，

sentences.en: we'll be able to use that to improve our navigation techniques.
sentences.zh: 我们就能利用它来改进我们的航海技术。

sentences.en: And so from there, he then...
sentences.zh: 从那里开始，他然后……

sentences.en: He gets secret orders, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他接到了秘密命令，对吧？

sentences.en: And he kind of opens up his letters and it tells him to go and discover Australia.
sentences.zh: 他拆开了信件，上面让他去发现澳大利亚。

sentences.en: He gets secret orders that he is to sail home via New Zealand,
sentences.zh: 他接到的秘密命令是经由新西兰航行回家，

sentences.en: which he circumnavigates and effectively, you know, improves on the charting of the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 他环绕了新西兰，实际上，你知道，改进了荷兰人的海图。

sentences.en: But also, people are interested in searching for Terra Australis.
sentences.zh: 但人们也对寻找“南方大陆”（Terra Australis）很感兴趣。

sentences.en: This is the great mythical counterweight continent that was meant to, according to Greek philosophers, stop the globe from tipping off its axis.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个伟大的神话中的平衡大陆，根据希腊哲学家的说法，它本应阻止地球从轴线上倾斜。

sentences.en: So Aristotle comes up with the brilliant idea once Pythagoras says, well, hey, the world's a globe.
sentences.zh: 所以亚里士多德提出了这个绝妙的想法，在毕达哥拉斯说“嘿，世界是个球体”之后。

sentences.en: Aristotle says, well, we've got a lot of land up here in where we are.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德说，好吧，我们在北边有很多陆地。

sentences.en: There must be some down south.
sentences.zh: 南边肯定也得有一些。

sentences.en: And so for much of the sort of 1400s, 1500s, 1600s, 1700s,
1700s, there was a desire among some of the European powers to find this great southern land.
sentences.zh: 1700年代，一些欧洲强权渴望找到这片伟大的南方大陆。

sentences.en: And certainly, after exploring New Zealand, he decides that he will sail home by the eastern coast of New Holland, as Australia was known.
sentences.zh: 当然，在探索完新西兰后，他决定沿着新荷兰（当时澳大利亚的称呼）的东海岸航行回家。

sentences.en: So it was obvious that he didn't discover Australia because he says,
sentences.zh: 所以很明显他并没有“发现”澳大利亚，因为他说，

sentences.en: I'm going to go there in my boat.
sentences.zh: “我要坐船去那里”。

sentences.en: And in 1770, and this is one of the great stories of Australian history,
sentences.zh: 而在1770年，这是澳大利亚历史上最伟大的故事之一，

sentences.en: the Cook's Landing Place at Botany Bay honours him for landing there on the 28th of April, 1770, even though he doesn't arrive there until the following afternoon.
sentences.zh: 植物学湾的库克登陆点纪念他于1770年4月28日在此登陆，尽管他直到第二天下午才到达那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And this date has not been corrected on the official monument for 151 years.
sentences.zh: 而这个日期在官方纪念碑上151年来都没有被纠正过。

sentences.en: But David, in Britain, we find Australian days really confusing.
sentences.zh: 但是大卫，在英国，我们觉得澳大利亚的日期真的很让人困惑。

sentences.en: I can never remember whether you're ahead or...
sentences.zh: 我永远记不住你们是超前还是……

sentences.en: So that's obviously what it is.
sentences.zh: 所以这显然就是原因所在。

sentences.en: We'll put it down to British dating era.
sentences.zh: 我们把它归咎于英国的日期错误吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But is it right that no European has landed at Botany Bay, at least?
sentences.zh: 但说没有欧洲人登陆过植物学湾，至少是这样，对吗？

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 那是对的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he's the first European to land there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是第一个登陆那里的欧洲人。

sentences.en: Look, there's no evidence of any European exploration of the east coast of Australia before 1770.
sentences.zh: 听着，没有证据表明在1770年之前有任何欧洲人探索过澳大利亚东海岸。

sentences.en: The French ran into the Great Barrier Reef a few years earlier and turned tail.
sentences.zh: 法国人几年前撞上了大堡礁，然后就掉头跑了。

sentences.en: Well, it's been often taught in the Australian school history curricula that the Portuguese were bobbing off the coast of eastern Australia in the 1520s
sentences.zh: 嗯，澳大利亚学校的历史课程中经常教导说，葡萄牙人在1520年代就在澳大利亚东海岸附近晃荡，

sentences.en: and left behind a vast mahogany ship that is buried in the dunes near the sleepy town of Warrnambool.
sentences.zh: 并留下了一艘巨大的红木船，埋在瓦南布尔那个安静小镇附近的沙丘里。

sentences.en: But that theory has largely been discredited and there's no real proof.
sentences.zh: 但那个理论在很大程度上已被推翻，并没有真正的证据。

sentences.en: Have they found the ship?
sentences.zh: 他们找到那艘船了吗？

sentences.en: Well, there is believed to be some sort of vessel there in the dunes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，人们认为沙丘里确实有某种船只。

sentences.en: At one stage when the sand shifted, something that looked rather like a barge rather than a 16th century Portuguese or 15th century,
sentences.zh: 有一次沙子移动时，露出了看起来更像驳船的东西，而不是16世纪的葡萄牙船，或者15世纪、

sentences.en: 16th century Portuguese caravel made of mahogany.
sentences.zh: 16世纪的葡萄牙红木帆船。

sentences.en: When you look at the stories that appeared in the newspapers, the guy who's often credited with discovering it was an Irishman, known for their tall tales in Australia.
sentences.zh: 当你查看报纸上的报道时，那个经常被认为发现它的人是个爱尔兰人，而爱尔兰人在澳大利亚以吹牛闻名。

sentences.en: The time where he claims to have actually discovered it, he appears to have been sitting in a peat hut somewhere in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 在他声称发现它的那个时间点，他似乎正坐在爱尔兰某处的泥炭小屋里。

sentences.en: So you automatically sort of discredit the accuracy of the story.
sentences.zh: 所以你自然会怀疑这个故事的准确性。

sentences.en: There were two bits, reported bits of the mahogany ship were collected by a bloke called Archibald, who was the editor of a leading Australian magazine,
sentences.zh: 当时有两个据称是红木船的碎片被一个叫阿奇博尔德的人收集起来，他是澳大利亚一家主要杂志的编辑，

sentences.en: donated to the Australian National Library.
sentences.zh: 并捐赠给了澳大利亚国家图书馆。

sentences.en: And they've been later tested and found to be made of eucalyptus, a tree that was in fairly short supply in Portugal in the 1500s.
sentences.zh: 后来经过检测，发现它们是桉木做的，这种树在1500年代的葡萄牙相当稀缺。

sentences.en: So let's sort of pull back a bit then.
sentences.zh: 那我们稍微退一步讲。

sentences.en: So Cook is supposed to have arrived at this date in Bosnian Bay.
sentences.zh: 所以库克被认为是在这个日期到达了植物学湾。

sentences.en: There's a statue of Cook, but obviously he's not the first human being to have discovered Australia.
sentences.zh: 那里有库克的雕像，但显然他不是第一个发现澳大利亚的人类。

sentences.en: So how long have human beings been in Australia before Captain Cook?
sentences.zh: 那么在库克船长之前，人类在澳大利亚生活了多久？

sentences.en: Well, we've actually, we've got a massive question here from Rachel Everett-Gouache.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们这里有一个来自蕾切尔·埃弗雷特-古阿什的重大问题。

sentences.en: I hope I've pronounced that right.
sentences.zh: 希望我没念错名字。

sentences.en: How did people get there?
sentences.zh: 人们是怎么到达那里的？

sentences.en: When did they get there?
sentences.zh: 他们是什么时候到达的？

sentences.en: How long did it take to occupy such a fast area?
sentences.zh: 占领如此广阔的区域花了多长时间？

sentences.en: So there are three massive questions.
sentences.zh: 所以这是三个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: The great thing about history is, of course, it's contestable.
sentences.zh: 历史的伟大之处当然在于它是可以争论的。

sentences.en: Pre-history, for want of a better term, is even more contestable.
sentences.zh: 史前史，如果用这个词的话，争议就更大了。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, we were taught that Aboriginal people had been on the continent for about 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，学校教导我们说原住民在大陆上生活了大约10000年。

sentences.en: The date that is commonly accepted now is around 60,000 to 65,000 years.
sentences.zh: 现在普遍接受的日期大约是60000到65000年。

sentences.en: Some people push that back to 120,000 years.
sentences.zh: 有些人将其推迟到120000年。

sentences.en: But there's a broad consensus of 65,000, give or take a couple of millennia.
sentences.zh: 但普遍共识是65000年，误差不过几千年。

sentences.en: So this is Homo sapiens coming out of Africa, crossing Asia, going down, cross the islands.
sentences.zh: 所以这是智人走出非洲，穿越亚洲，南下，跨过岛屿。

sentences.en: Of course, Aboriginal people, some Aboriginal people maintain that they were created here and they've always been here.
sentences.zh: 当然，原住民，一些原住民坚持认为他们是在这里被创造出来的，他们一直都在这里。

sentences.en: But the scientific evidence would support the out of Africa thesis that they effectively island hopped from Sunda, as sort of Southeast Asia was known,
sentences.zh: 但科学证据支持“走出非洲”的论点，即他们实际上是从巽他古陆（当时东南亚的称呼）跳岛而来，

sentences.en: to the continental landmass of Sahul, which took in Australia and New Guinea.
sentences.zh: 到达了萨胡尔大陆，其中包括澳大利亚和新几内亚。

sentences.en: Sea levels were between 70 and 140 metres lower than they are now.
sentences.zh: 当时的海平面比现在低70到140米。

sentences.en: Is that because all the water's locked up in ice?
sentences.zh: 这是因为所有的水都被锁在冰里了吗？

sentences.en: Is this during the ice ages?
sentences.zh: 这是在冰河时代吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, during one of the ice ages.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，在其中一个冰河时代。

sentences.en: So you could sort of walk around New Guinea, Australia, Tasmania were part of one landmass.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以步行往返于新几内亚、澳大利亚和塔斯马尼亚，它们曾是同一块陆地。

sentences.en: They were obviously a seafaring people because to get across the Sunda Strait and to get across the Wallace Line that separates Bali and Lombok,
sentences.zh: 他们显然是航海民族，因为要穿过巽他海峡，要穿过分隔巴厘岛和龙目岛的华莱士线，

sentences.en: it's a deep ocean trench that the big, scary animals of Asia had never been able to get across.
sentences.zh: 那是一条深海沟，亚洲那些大型可怕的动物从来没能跨越过去。

sentences.en: So no tigers in Lombok.
sentences.zh: 所以龙目岛上没有老虎。

sentences.en: And so when the first Australians would have crossed that line, they would have suddenly found this sort of land where there were no large prey animals intent on eating them.
sentences.zh: 所以，当第一批澳大利亚人跨过那条线时，他们会突然发现这片土地上没有那种一心想吃掉他们的大型猎食动物。

sentences.en: But there were lots of animals that had never seen humans before that basically sat there and you could club them over their head and have a jolly good meal.
sentences.zh: 但这里有很多从未见过人类的动物，它们基本上就待在那儿，你可以一棍子敲晕它们，然后美餐一顿。

sentences.en: So that was probably the first experience of Australia around about 65,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，这大概就是大约65000年前人类在澳大利亚的最初体验。

sentences.en: But in Australia then, I mean, there are extraordinary animals and so there is, there's the marsupial lion.
sentences.zh: 但在当时的澳大利亚，我的意思是，这里有非凡的动物，比如袋狮。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: Supposedly kind of lurks in trees.
sentences.zh: 据说它们会潜伏在树上。

sentences.en: Phybocoleocarnifex.
sentences.zh: 袋狮（Thylacoleo carnifex）。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I went to Adelaide and saw a skeleton of it in the museum there and it looked very menacing and you wouldn't want to have it drop out on top of you from a tree.
sentences.zh: 我去过阿德莱德，在当地博物馆见过它的骨架，看起来非常凶猛，你肯定不想让它从树上掉到你身上。

sentences.en: No, they got up to about 130 kilos.
sentences.zh: 没错，它们体重可达130公斤左右。

sentences.en: They're believed to be ambush predators.
sentences.zh: 人们认为它们是伏击型捕食者。

sentences.en: Their muscular suggests that they perhaps weren't great runners, but, you know, they're effectively the size of a panther or a leopard that would leap out and take a nibble of you.
sentences.zh: 它们的肌肉结构表明它们可能不擅长奔跑，但你知道，它们实际上有豹子那么大，会跳出来咬你一口。

sentences.en: Dennis, Lily-esque predator to have jumping on you.
sentences.zh: 丹尼斯，这可真是个莉莉式的捕食者，要是跳到你身上可不得了。

sentences.en: We've had lots of questions about this, haven't we?
sentences.zh: 我们收到过很多关于这方面的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: So the Kanzuk kid and others have asked about, I mean, all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 比如Kanzuk kid和其他人问过，我的意思是，各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: Land crocodiles, giant koalas.
sentences.zh: 陆地鳄鱼、巨型考拉。

sentences.en: Ah, yes.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的。

sentences.en: Giant kangaroos.
sentences.zh: 巨型袋鼠。

sentences.en: Are these things real?
sentences.zh: 这些东西是真的吗？

sentences.en: Do they really exist?
sentences.zh: 它们真的存在吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, look, megafauna, as they're known, which is Latin for really big animal.
sentences.zh: 所以，听着，巨型动物群（Megafauna），正如它们的名字所暗示的那样，在拉丁语里就是“真正的大动物”。

sentences.en: We, yeah, look, Australia had its own megafauna.
sentences.zh: 我们，是的，你看，澳大利亚有它自己的巨型动物群。

sentences.en: The land crocodile, the quincana, is one of my favourites.
sentences.zh: 陆地鳄鱼，也就是澳洲古鳄（Quincana），是我最喜欢的动物之一。

sentences.en: It grows up to maybe seven metres in length.
sentences.zh: 它能长到七米长。

sentences.en: It's got – its legs are underneath it for walking on land rather than at its sides for paddling.
sentences.zh: 它的腿长在身体下方，是为了在陆地上行走，而不是像其他鳄鱼那样长在两侧用来划水。

sentences.en: And fossils have been found in areas near no known watercourses.
sentences.zh: 而且在远离已知水道的地区也发现了它们的化石。

sentences.en: So, you know, you British tourists are afraid of all sorts of animals in Australia, particularly those in our waterways.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你们这些英国游客害怕澳大利亚的各种动物，尤其是那些生活在水道里的。

sentences.en: This was actually one that you could be scared of on land as well.
sentences.zh: 但这实际上是一种你在陆地上也会感到害怕的动物。

sentences.en: I didn't like the way you said you began that sentence with such contempt, you British tourists.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢你刚才说那句话时那种轻蔑的语气，“你们这些英国游客”。

sentences.en: Well, it's always the first question we're asked is about our animals.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们被问到的第一个问题总是关于我们的动物。

sentences.en: But giant koalas – look, there was a koala only about a third larger than our current koala.
sentences.zh: 但巨型考拉——你看，有一种考拉只比我们现在的考拉大三分之一左右。

sentences.en: We in Australia have legends of the drop bear, basically designed to frighten tourists of giant koalas that drop from the trees.
sentences.zh: 我们在澳大利亚有关于“掉落熊”（drop bear）的传说，这基本上是为了吓唬游客，说有巨型考拉会从树上掉下来。

sentences.en: No evidence of the drop bear.
sentences.zh: 没有证据表明存在“掉落熊”。

sentences.en: My favourite – there was, of course, the diprotodon, which was the largeSt.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的是——当然，还有双门齿兽（Diprotodon），它是最大的。

sentences.en: Yes, the giant wombat.
sentences.zh: 是的，巨型袋熊。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: It's sort of a rhinoceros-sized wombat-like creature.
sentences.zh: 它是一种犀牛大小、类似袋熊的生物。

sentences.en: And one of the things about Australia is that its land is incredibly arid, limited nutrients in plants.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚的一个特点是土地极其干旱，植物中的营养成分有限。

sentences.en: And lots of the large marsupials here, pouched animals, to conserve energy, their brain pan or their brain devolved.
sentences.zh: 这里许多大型有袋动物为了节省能量，它们的脑壳或大脑退化了。

sentences.en: So, you have something – So, you're saying they're thick?
sentences.zh: 所以，你是指——你是说它们很笨？

sentences.en: They were remarkably thick.
sentences.zh: 它们确实非常笨。

sentences.en: The koala today, its brain has shriveled so that it effectively gets concussion every time it turns its head.
sentences.zh: 今天的考拉，它的大脑已经萎缩，以至于每次转头时实际上都会脑震荡。

sentences.en: Oh, that's adorable.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太可爱了。

sentences.en: Because it's trying to save energy.
sentences.zh: 因为它是为了节省能量。

sentences.en: But look, it's too whacked out on gum leaves to really notice.
sentences.zh: 但你看，它吃桉树叶吃得太嗨了，根本没注意到。

sentences.en: But the diprotodon, again, large skull, large sinuses, small brain.
sentences.zh: 但双门齿兽，同样是头骨大、鼻窦大、大脑小。

sentences.en: So, old koalas would be gutted by the degeneracy of their descendants.
sentences.zh: 所以，老一辈的考拉会被它们后代的退化所伤害。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没错。

sentences.en: We Australians have obviously evolved smaller brains in the last 200 years.
sentences.zh: 我们澳大利亚人在过去200年里显然进化出了更小的大脑。

sentences.en: Just on diprotodon.
sentences.zh: 就说双门齿兽吧。

sentences.en: Just on diprotodon, which is this enormous wombat.
sentences.zh: 就说双门齿兽，也就是这种巨大的袋熊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wombats, famously, their poos are square.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，袋熊的粪便是方形的。

sentences.en: A square.
sentences.zh: 方形的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Did diprotodon do kind of like – do we know?
sentences.zh: 双门齿兽也是这样吗——我们知道吗？

sentences.en: Did he do enormous square-shaped turds?
sentences.zh: 它会排出巨大的方形粪便吗？

sentences.en: There is actually a field of study from which you can date when the megafauna may have died out,
sentences.zh: 实际上有一个研究领域可以通过观察澳大利亚食草动物粪便中的真菌来推断巨型动物群可能灭绝的时间，

sentences.en: which is looking at the fungus that could be found in the poos of herbivorous animals in Australia.
sentences.zh: 也就是观察在粪便中发现的真菌。

sentences.en: There's no suggestion that the diprotodon had a square arsehole.
sentences.zh: 没有任何迹象表明双门齿兽有一个方形的肛门。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a shame.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: That's a shame.
sentences.zh: 太遗憾了。

sentences.en: Look, I mean, my favourite example of the megafauna is known by archaeologists and naturalists affectionately as the demon duck of doom.
sentences.zh: 你看，我最喜欢的巨型动物群例子被考古学家和博物学家亲切地称为“末日恶魔鸭”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Bullochus planae, which is basically a quarter-ton, eight-foot-tall, carnivorous, kick-ass duck.
sentences.zh: 平原牛顿巨鸟（Bullochornis planei），基本上是一只四分之一吨重、八英尺高、肉食性的、厉害的鸭子。

sentences.en: So it probably had died out before the first Australian humans appeared.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能在第一批澳大利亚人类出现之前就已经灭绝了。

sentences.en: Can I just ask specifically about humans arriving and the megafauna?
sentences.zh: 我可以专门问一下人类到达与巨型动物群之间的关系吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: The megafauna is no longer around.
sentences.zh: 巨型动物群已经不存在了。

sentences.en: Humans have arrived.
sentences.zh: 人类已经到达。

sentences.en: Is there a link?
sentences.zh: 这之间有联系吗？

sentences.en: Basically, are humans killing out – wiping out all these giant animals?
sentences.zh: 基本上，是人类杀死了——消灭了所有这些巨型动物吗？

sentences.en: And it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: This is one of the sort of politically contested bits of Australian history.
sentences.zh: 这是澳大利亚历史上在政治上有争议的部分之一。

sentences.en: Because the idea is that Aboriginal Australians have cared for the land in a way that repatriates Europeans haven't.
sentences.zh: 因为人们认为澳大利亚原住民以一种欧洲殖民者没有的方式关爱着这片土地。

sentences.en: Rather than eating all the big animals and burnt many of the forests.
sentences.zh: 而不是吃光所有大型动物并烧毁许多森林。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Look, the jury remains out.
sentences.zh: 你看，目前还没有定论。

sentences.en: There's no doubt that some of the megafauna co-existed with humans for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，一些巨型动物群与人类共存了一段时间。

sentences.en: The length of time is contested.
sentences.zh: 但持续时间是有争议的。

sentences.en: There appears to have been a significant megafaunal die-off about 40,000 to 44,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 大约在40000到44000年前，似乎发生了一次重大的巨型动物群灭绝事件。

sentences.en: And Tim Flannery, who wrote a wonderful book called The Future Eaters, has the blitzkrieg theory of megafaunal extinction, which is essentially when humans arrived in Australia,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·弗兰纳里（Tim Flannery）写了一本很棒的书叫《未来食客》（The Future Eaters），他提出了巨型动物群灭绝的“闪电战理论”，本质上就是当人类到达澳大利亚时，

sentences.en: there were all these big animals with small brains that sat there and let you put them on the head.
sentences.zh: 有这么多大脑很小的大型动物待在那儿，任由你敲它们的头。

sentences.en: And said, eat me.
sentences.zh: 仿佛在说，吃我吧。

sentences.en: And so, you know, people had really big barbecues for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，人们举办了很长时间的超大型烧烤派对。

sentences.en: And once the megafauna died out, there was a move to the hunting of smaller animals and the firing of forests to flush them out onto grasslands.
sentences.zh: 而一旦巨型动物群灭绝，人们就开始转向狩猎小型动物，并焚烧森林将它们驱赶到草原上。

sentences.en: And there's a suggestion, according to that theory, that Aboriginal people fundamentally changed the Australian landscape to hunt for smaller food prey.
sentences.zh: 根据该理论，有人认为原住民从根本上改变了澳大利亚的景观，以猎取更小的猎物。

sentences.en: The alternative theory is that climate change played a significant impact.
sentences.zh: 另一种理论是气候变化产生了重大影响。

sentences.en: Is there a sense in which this argument is driven by politics, or would that be an overly reductive way of framing it?
sentences.zh: 这种争论在某种程度上是由政治驱动的吗？还是说这种说法过于简化了？

sentences.en: No, look, it's a debate that moves backwards and forwards.
sentences.zh: 不，你看，这是一场来回反复的辩论。

sentences.en: And look, there were probably pockets of megafauna that survived until relatively recent times.
sentences.zh: 而且你看，可能有一些巨型动物群在相对较近的时期内幸存了下来。

sentences.en: There's the Bradshaw paintings or the Guéon Guéon paintings in Arnhem Land in the north of Australia, which are probably dated about 17,500 years ago.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚北部的阿纳姆地（Arnhem Land）有布拉德肖岩画（Bradshaw paintings）或古恩古恩岩画（Guion Guion paintings），其年代可能在17500年前左右。

sentences.en: There's a couple of them that feature what appears to be a marsupial lion.
sentences.zh: 其中有几幅画描绘了看起来像是袋狮的动物。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it kind of looks like Tigger, doesn't it, from Winnie the Blue?
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像跳跳虎，对吧，来自《小熊维尼》？

sentences.en: It does, yeah, or the tiger from Calvin and Hobbes, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实，或者像《卡尔文与霍布斯》里的老虎，是的。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, that's right, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，没错，是的。

sentences.en: A striped dog-like creature that could be a thylacine, the Tasmanian tiger, which the last ones died out in Australia in the 1930s, down in Tasmania.
sentences.zh: 一种条纹状的犬类生物，可能是袋狼，也就是塔斯马尼亚虎，最后一只在20世纪30年代死于塔斯马尼亚。

sentences.en: Or did they?
sentences.zh: 或者它们真的灭绝了吗？

sentences.en: Or did they?
sentences.zh: 或者它们真的灭绝了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，哦，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, there's a whole episode in that.
sentences.zh: 哦，那里面有一整集的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, we must get down that one.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们一定要深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: Let's get back to the Aborigines.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到原住民的话题。

sentences.en: So you're talking, all the theories about what they did, I mean, those obviously rest on some sense of what their culture might have been.
sentences.zh: 所以你谈到的所有关于他们行为的理论，我的意思是，这些显然建立在对他们文化可能是什么样子的某种认知之上。

sentences.en: So when we're talking about the first Australians, let's say 50,000, 40,000 years ago, are we basing that on specific archaeological evidence?
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论第一批澳大利亚人时，比如50000、40000年前，我们是基于具体的考古证据吗？

sentences.en: Or are people extrapolating back from what they know of Aboriginal society in the 18th century or whenever?
sentences.zh: 还是人们根据他们对18世纪或任何时期原住民社会的了解进行推断？

sentences.en: A number of different factors.
sentences.zh: 这是多种因素共同作用的结果。

sentences.en: I mean, radiocarbon dating, sort of you can get 40,000, 50,000 years back before it stops being effective.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，放射性碳测年法，大约能回溯到40000、50000年前，再久远就失效了。

sentences.en: Mungo Man is the sort of oldest body of an Aboriginal person that dates to about 40,000 BP.
sentences.zh: 蒙哥人（Mungo Man）是已知最古老的原住民遗骸，距今约40000年。

sentences.en: It's also the earliest example in the world that's known of ritual burial, where the body is buried with ochre paint sprinkled upon it.
sentences.zh: 这也是世界上已知的最早的仪式性埋葬案例，尸体被埋葬时上面撒有赭石颜料。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you've got earlier dating of stone implements through sort of luminescent technology, which can calculate how old something is by when it was sort of heated in a fire,
sentences.zh: 所以你通过发光测年技术对石器进行了更早的测年，这种技术可以通过计算某物在火中加热的时间来计算其年代，

sentences.en: as some early stone tools were.
sentences.zh: 正如一些早期石器所做的那样。

sentences.en: And you've got some genetic dating, which suggests somewhere between 60 and 75,000 years ago as a timeline that sort of genetically fits.
sentences.zh: 还有一些基因测年，表明大约60000到75000年前是一个在基因上吻合的时间线。

sentences.en: But beyond those things, can we say anything more sort of, I mean, obviously we know that there were people there,
sentences.zh: 但除了这些，我们还能说些什么呢？我的意思是，显然我们知道那里有人，

sentences.en: but can we say anything about the kind of society that they had or their religion or their family structures or any of those kinds of things?
sentences.zh: 但我们能说出关于他们的社会、宗教、家庭结构或任何这类事情吗？

sentences.en: We certainly know in recent millennia what those things were like.
sentences.zh: 我们当然知道最近几千年来这些情况是什么样的。

sentences.en: I mean, you have over 250 languages, so you have a period of time for dispersal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有超过250种语言，所以你有足够的时间进行扩散。

sentences.en: You have most of Australia with one language group, with different languages within that group, and more completely different languages in the north,
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚大部分地区属于一个语族，该语族内有不同的语言，而在北部则有更多完全不同的语言，

sentences.en: which may coincide with an infusion of Indian settlement several thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 这可能与几千年前印度移民的涌入相吻合。

sentences.en: And is it thought that the original wave of arrival of humans, say 60,000 years ago, is that basically the group from which all the Aboriginal peoples in Australia descend,
sentences.zh: 那么，人们是否认为人类最初到达的那一波，比如60000年前，基本上就是所有澳大利亚原住民的祖先群体，

sentences.en: or are there waves of people coming?
sentences.zh: 还是说有几波人陆续到来？

sentences.en: What's the thinking on that?
sentences.zh: 对此有什么看法？

sentences.en: Yeah, there's the single wave theory and the multi-wave theory.
sentences.zh: 是的，有单波理论和多波理论。

sentences.en: And the single wave theory says that with the genetic diversity that you have in Australia,
sentences.zh: 单波理论认为，考虑到澳大利亚现有的遗传多样性，

sentences.en: you would have had to have had about between 1,000 and 3,000 people come across about 65,000 years ago to have the genetic diversity that you have with the first Australians at the time of first contact.
sentences.zh: 大约65000年前必须有1000到3000人跨海而来，才能拥有第一批澳大利亚人在首次接触时所具备的遗传多样性。

sentences.en: We know that the Lapita people, the sort of proto-Polynesian seafarers, probably stopped off and gave us the dingo sort of 4,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们知道拉皮塔人（Lapita people），即原始波利尼西亚航海家，可能在大约4000年前中途停留并给我们带来了澳洲野犬。

sentences.en: There are suggestions of some Indian genetic admixture in the north of Australia again around that 5,000-year mark.
sentences.zh: 有迹象表明，大约在5000年前，澳大利亚北部再次出现了一些印度基因混合。

sentences.en: So, the multi-wave theory is that there were, if you can have one group of people coming over, why can't you have two, three, four, five or more?
sentences.zh: 所以，多波理论认为，如果可以有一群人过来，为什么不能有两群、三群、四群、五群或更多呢？

sentences.en: That is, there is some political and cultural arguments associated with that, which suggests that people who are Aboriginal today were perhaps invaded by other people,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这其中存在一些政治和文化上的争论，有人认为今天的原住民可能是被其他人入侵的，

sentences.en: rather than having been there all the time and the first owners.
sentences.zh: 而不是一直待在那里作为第一主人。

sentences.en: So, it's contested.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是有争议的。

sentences.en: So, there's a question here from the Burning Archive.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个来自“燃烧的档案”（Burning Archive）的问题。

sentences.en: It is sometimes said these days, Aboriginal culture is the oldest continuous culture in the world.
sentences.zh: 如今人们常说，原住民文化是世界上最古老的连续文化。

sentences.en: Is this true?
sentences.zh: 这是真的吗？

sentences.en: How could we know?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么可能知道？

sentences.en: How could we know is a very good question.
sentences.zh: “我们怎么可能知道”是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What you can say is that some of the Aboriginal Dreamtime stories suggest a continual culture and oral tradition that is many, many millennia old.
sentences.zh: 你可以说，一些原住民的“梦幻时光”（Dreamtime）故事暗示了一种延续至今的文化和口头传统，已经有许多许多个千年了。

sentences.en: There are stories of creatures that sound like megafauna in some of the Aboriginal Dreamtime stories.
sentences.zh: 在一些原住民的“梦幻时光”故事中，有关于听起来像巨型动物群的生物的故事。

sentences.en: Is that the bunyip?
sentences.zh: 那是本耶普（bunyip）吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the bunyip, which is meant to be a grumpy creature that inhabits waterholes that we Australians call billabongs,
sentences.zh: 是的，本耶普，据说是一种脾气暴躁的生物，栖息在我们澳大利亚人称为比拉邦（billabong）的水潭中，

sentences.en: may trace its origins to the diprotodons that used to sort of wade in sort of marshland.
sentences.zh: 其起源可能追溯到过去在沼泽地里涉水的双门齿兽。

sentences.en: There are also a range of stories of very large animals that gathered and gathered in the trees, perhaps, which is where the giant koala theory comes from,
sentences.zh: 还有一系列关于非常大的动物聚集在树上的故事，这可能就是巨型考拉理论的来源，

sentences.en: that may trace back to a megafauna type creature.
sentences.zh: 这可能追溯到某种巨型动物群生物。

sentences.en: But also there are particular stories in very arid parts of Australia of a landscape that was radically different, much more fertile,
sentences.zh: 但同时，在澳大利亚非常干旱的地区，也有一些关于景观截然不同、更加肥沃的特定故事，

sentences.en: and stories that really seem to be tracing back for people who've been in the same place for a while to quite a different climate.
sentences.zh: 这些故事似乎确实是在追溯那些在同一个地方生活了很久的人们对完全不同气候的记忆。

sentences.en: Before we go, we have to have a break in a minute or two, but just before we do that, the Dreamtime stories,
sentences.zh: 在继续之前，我们得休息一两分钟，但在休息之前，关于“梦幻时代”的故事，

sentences.en: can you tell us a little bit about what they are and how we know about them and how we know that they are kind of authentic or continuous rather than, you know,
sentences.zh: 你能给我们讲讲它们到底是什么，我们是如何了解它们的，以及我们如何确定它们是某种真实或连续的，而不是，你知道的，

sentences.en: so much folklore tends to be invented or sort of elaborated upon and of course changes over time.
sentences.zh: 很多民间传说往往是虚构的，或者经过了某种润色，当然也会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: So Dreamtime stories, tell us a little bit more about them.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于“梦幻时代”的故事，再多给我们讲讲吧。

sentences.en: a form of mnemonic device to navigate around your bit of the continent.
sentences.zh: 这是一种用于在大陆特定区域导航的助记手段。

sentences.en: But the idea of the Dreamtime, Aboriginal history is very different from a Western history where we focus on progress.
sentences.zh: 但“梦幻时代”的概念，与我们关注进步的西方历史中的原住民历史非常不同。

sentences.en: Aboriginal cultures focused on continuity and stability.
sentences.zh: 原住民文化关注的是连续性和稳定性。

sentences.en: And the Dreamtime stories were, if you like, a way of codifying rules and laws.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，“梦幻时代”的故事是一种编纂规则和法律的方式。

sentences.en: They had supernatural elements.
sentences.zh: 它们包含超自然元素。

sentences.en: We know that modern Aboriginal people had sort of animist religious spiritual beliefs, that their ancestors inhabited rocks and trees of significance.
sentences.zh: 我们知道现代原住民拥有某种万物有灵的宗教信仰，他们的祖先居住在重要的岩石和树木中。

sentences.en: And so you have this complex series of laws, cultural traditions, stories about who you can marry and who you can't marry.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一套复杂的法律、文化传统，以及关于你可以和谁结婚、不能和谁结婚的故事。

sentences.en: And it was beautifully summed up by an Australian anthropologist, Bill Stanner, who described the sort of dreamtime as timeless, described it as every when.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚人类学家比尔·斯坦纳对此做了精辟的总结，他将“梦幻时代”描述为永恒的，描述为“无处不在的时间”。

sentences.en: So it's this fusing of spirituality with the past, present and the future into sort of a series of stories as to how life is to be lived and life is to be regulated.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一种将灵性与过去、现在和未来融合在一起的故事系列，讲述了生活该如何度过，生活该如何被规范。

sentences.en: And when were they written down by non-Aboriginals?
sentences.zh: 那么它们是什么时候被非原住民记录下来的呢？

sentences.en: So were they recorded in the 19th century or how does that work?
sentences.zh: 它们是在19世纪被记录的吗？还是说情况如何？

sentences.en: And look, this is one of the tricky bits.
sentences.zh: 听着，这是棘手的部分之一。

sentences.en: Often, white explorers weren't terribly interested in sitting down and listening to Aboriginal stories.
sentences.zh: 通常，白人探险家对坐下来倾听原住民的故事并不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: They were far more interested in chasing Aboriginal people off the land they were trying to put their sheep on.
sentences.zh: 他们更感兴趣的是把原住民从他们想放牧的土地上赶走。

sentences.en: So certainly there are, particularly Aboriginal creation myths,
sentences.zh: 所以当然有，特别是原住民的创世神话，

sentences.en: they were collected because missionaries who were interested in spreading the word of God were trying to tap into what do you have there in terms of creation mythology.
sentences.zh: 它们被收集起来是因为那些热衷于传播上帝福音的传教士，试图挖掘你们在创世神话方面有什么内容。

sentences.en: So you have many Aboriginal cultures have got a giant snake-like creator figure that is associated with water that Westerners named the Rainbow Serpent that appears throughout Australia.
sentences.zh: 所以很多原住民文化中都有一个与水有关的巨大蛇形创造者形象，西方人称之为“彩虹蛇”，它出现在整个澳大利亚。

sentences.en: Down in Tasmania, the Tasmanian Aboriginal people of Bruny Island had a creator named Lala who appears to have been a giant ant.
sentences.zh: 在塔斯马尼亚，布鲁尼岛的塔斯马尼亚原住民有一个名叫拉拉的创造者，它似乎是一只巨大的蚂蚁。

sentences.en: So there was some recording of these stories,
sentences.zh: 所以这些故事确实有一些记录，

sentences.en: but the best records you would have would be with Aboriginal people who wrote those stories down themselves in the late 19th and the early 20th century and who continued to tell those stories orally.
sentences.zh: 但你所能拥有的最好的记录，是那些在19世纪末和20世纪初亲自写下这些故事，并继续以口头方式讲述这些故事的原住民所留下的。

sentences.en: And just one last question before we go to a break.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，最后一个问题。

sentences.en: Do you think, did Aboriginal peoples in Australia have a sense of themselves as belonging to this kind of the same group of people or do they have no sense of that at all?
sentences.zh: 你认为，澳大利亚的原住民是否有一种归属于同一个群体的自我认同感？还是说他们完全没有这种感觉？

sentences.en: Is that a kind of a colonial imposition?
sentences.zh: 这是一种殖民强加的概念吗？

sentences.en: So that's, look, the entire notion of Aboriginality is a colonial construct.
sentences.zh: 听着，整个“原住民性”的概念就是一个殖民建构。

sentences.en: I mean, Australia is, you know, the size of Western Europe plus some.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，澳大利亚的面积，你知道的，相当于西欧加上其他一些地方。

sentences.en: It's like saying, you know, do the Poles and the Cornish regard each other as similar?
sentences.zh: 这就像是问，你知道的，波兰人和康沃尔人是否认为彼此相似？

sentences.en: You have over 250 language groups.
sentences.zh: 你有超过250个语言群体。

sentences.en: Within those language groups, you have up to 50 clans, as low as, you know, just a handful of clans.
sentences.zh: 在这些语言群体中，有多达50个氏族，也有少到只有几个氏族的。

sentences.en: So these people did not see each other as part of the same people.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人并不认为彼此是同一个民族的一部分。

sentences.en: That being said, there was trade and communication across the continent.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，整个大陆上确实存在贸易和交流。

sentences.en: You have shells from northern Queensland appearing in Western Australia where they were passed on as trade goods.
sentences.zh: 来自昆士兰北部的贝壳出现在西澳大利亚，它们被当作贸易商品传递过去。

sentences.en: So you have communication and trade occurring over large distances.
sentences.zh: 所以你确实有跨越长距离的交流和贸易发生。

sentences.en: But there was certainly not the belief we are all Aboriginal people.
sentences.zh: 但肯定不存在“我们都是原住民”这种信念。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, I think we should go for a break now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在该休息一下了。

sentences.en: And when we come back, perhaps we could look at the process by which Europeans and perhaps Chinese.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，也许我们可以看看欧洲人，或许还有中国人，来到这里的过程。

sentences.en: Oh, oh, good.
sentences.zh: 哦，哦，好。

sentences.en: I like that bit.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那部分。

sentences.en: We'll be back in a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们一会儿回来。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余韵》。

sentences.en: We are talking about Australia.
sentences.zh: 我们正在谈论澳大利亚。

sentences.en: And in particular, we've been talking about Australia before the arrival of the first Europeans or indeed the first British.
sentences.zh: 特别是，我们一直在谈论第一批欧洲人，或者说第一批英国人到达之前的澳大利亚。

sentences.en: So, David, the first outsiders, as in non-Aboriginal peoples, to arrive in Australia.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，第一批外来者，也就是非原住民，到达澳大利亚的情况。

sentences.en: Now, in Britain, we were always brought up to think that this is Captain Cook followed by boatloads of convicts.
sentences.zh: 在英国，我们从小就被教育认为这是库克船长，随后是满载囚犯的船只。

sentences.en: But we've got a question from, for example, Novasluf, one of our listeners,
sentences.zh: 但我们有一个问题，比如来自我们的听众之一诺瓦斯卢夫，

sentences.en: who asks about contact between Indonesians and Malayans or the people who lived in what are now Indonesia and Malaya.
sentences.zh: 他问到了印尼人和马来人，或者居住在现在的印尼和马来亚的人之间的接触。

sentences.en: So, are they arriving in Australia?
sentences.zh: 那么，他们到达过澳大利亚吗？

sentences.en: And if so, why don't they settle it and colonize it?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，为什么他们没有定居并殖民它？

sentences.en: So, there's evidence of the Macassans from the island of Sulawesi, which is modern-day Indonesia, fishermen who – the precise date is uncertain.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，来自苏拉威西岛（即现代印尼）的望加锡渔民——具体日期不确定。

sentences.en: It's certainly the early 1600s, probably in the 1500s.
sentences.zh: 肯定是在17世纪初，可能在16世纪。

sentences.en: And they were coming to the northern shores of Australia to fish for trepang, sea cucumber, which was prized in China as an aphrodisiac.
sentences.zh: 他们来到澳大利亚北部海岸捕捞海参，这种海参在中国被视为珍贵的春药。

sentences.en: So, that content was – that contact was – Australia was effectively an Asian sex shop.
sentences.zh: 所以，那种接触——澳大利亚实际上是一个亚洲性用品商店。

sentences.en: As people are coming here to get this very ugly creature.
sentences.zh: 因为人们来到这里获取这种非常丑陋的生物。

sentences.en: It's basically a black sausage that sits in shallow coastal waters and aspires to nothing more than not ending up in a Beijing sex shop.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是一根黑色的香肠，待在浅海沿岸，除了不想最终出现在北京的性用品商店外，别无所求。

sentences.en: And the Macassans –
sentences.zh: 而望加锡人——

sentences.en: What a life.
sentences.zh: 真是种生活。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: The Macassans came here and they form close cultural relations with the Yongle people in Arnhem Land and actually effectively buy their labor for this industry.
sentences.zh: 望加锡人来到这里，与阿纳姆地的雍古族人建立了密切的文化关系，实际上有效地购买了他们的劳动力来从事这个行业。

sentences.en: You have probably about a thousand Macassans coming here each season.
sentences.zh: 每个季节大约有一千名望加锡人来到这里。

sentences.en: They stay for months.
sentences.zh: 他们停留数月。

sentences.en: They build these sort of demountable factories where they process the trepang, the sea cucumber, it's boiled, it's dried, it's buried in the sand for a few weeks, it's dug up,
sentences.zh: 他们建造了这种可拆卸的工厂，在那里加工海参，煮沸、晒干、埋在沙子里几周，挖出来，

sentences.en: it's boiled, it's packaged and it's shipped off.
sentences.zh: 煮沸、包装，然后运走。

sentences.en: And they traded glass, cloth, metal implements, alcohol, and there was language exchange as well.
sentences.zh: 他们交易玻璃、布料、金属器具、酒精，也有语言交流。

sentences.en: So, when the first Europeans came to this part of Australia, when they appeared, the Aboriginal – the Yongle knew of them and they called them, ah, Belanda,
sentences.zh: 所以，当第一批欧洲人来到澳大利亚这一地区时，当他们出现时，原住民——雍古人知道他们，并称他们为“贝兰达”，

sentences.en: which was Hollander that they'd picked up from the Macassan people.
sentences.zh: 这是他们从望加锡人那里学来的“荷兰人”一词。

sentences.en: So, they had an idea that there were Europeans out there.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们知道外面有欧洲人存在。

sentences.en: But, yeah, that's the – other than the sort of Lapita proto-Polynesians who arrived about 4,000 years ago and dropped off the dingo, they are the first really established contacts.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，除了大约4000年前到达并留下了澳洲野犬的拉皮塔原波利尼西亚人之外，他们是第一批真正确立的接触者。

sentences.en: Why don't people come in greater numbers?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们没有以更大的规模前来？

sentences.en: Why don't – given the population in Southeast Asia and so on, and given that they are moving around in boats, they're seafaring peoples, why don't more people come to Australia?
sentences.zh: 为什么——考虑到东南亚的人口等等，考虑到他们是乘船移动的，他们是航海民族，为什么没有更多的人来到澳大利亚？

sentences.en: So, look, there is some Lapita DNA in some of the northern Torres Strait Islands and on the southern coast of New Guinea, predominantly Melanesian,
sentences.zh: 看，在托雷斯海峡北部的一些岛屿和新几内亚南海岸，确实有一些拉皮塔人的DNA，主要是美拉尼西亚人，

sentences.en: but some Polynesian influence as well.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些波利尼西亚的影响。

sentences.en: Well, I think the answer is nobody really knows.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想答案是没人真正知道。

sentences.en: There may have been – if you're coming in just a handful of boats and you encounter stiff resistance from some people who don't want you to stop there,
sentences.zh: 可能曾经有——如果你只乘几艘船前来，却遇到了不想让你停留的人的强烈抵抗，

sentences.en: as occurred in the Andaman Islands, you know, for centuries.
sentences.zh: 就像在安达曼群岛发生的那样，你知道，持续了几个世纪。

sentences.en: If you run into some territorial people who drive you off, maybe you don't want to stay.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到一些领土意识很强的人把你赶走，也许你就不想留下来了。

sentences.en: But there certainly was trade with the dingo and kangaroo fleas then appear to have got on dingoes that the Lapita then took to Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 但确实存在贸易，澳洲野犬和袋鼠跳蚤似乎就是在那时出现在了拉皮塔人带到东南亚的野犬身上。

sentences.en: So, you get kangaroo fleas and some native dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你得到了袋鼠跳蚤和一些本地狗。

sentences.en: So, Australia is exporting sex aphrodisiacs and fleas.
sentences.zh: 所以，澳大利亚出口的是春药和跳蚤。

sentences.en: And fleas.
sentences.zh: 还有跳蚤。

sentences.en: Fleas.
sentences.zh: 跳蚤。

sentences.en: Pretty much.
sentences.zh: 差不多吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, you're really selling it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你还真是卖力推销啊。

sentences.en: So, David, you mentioned China.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，你提到了中国。

sentences.en: Now, there is a theory, is there not, that the Chinese discovered Australia.
sentences.zh: 现在有一种理论，不是吗，说中国人发现了澳大利亚。

sentences.en: What do you make of that?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.en: If you're an Australian, it's a disturbing theory because in 2003, Premier Hugh Jintao became, I think,
sentences.zh: 如果你是澳大利亚人，这是一个令人不安的理论，因为在2003年，胡锦涛主席成为了，我想，

sentences.en: just the second non-Australian to address both houses of parliament and basically said, look, we were here in the 1420s engaging in harmonious relations with the locals.
sentences.zh: 第二位在澳大利亚议会两院发表演讲的非澳大利亚人，他基本上说，看，我们在1420年代就来到这里，与当地人保持着和谐的关系。

sentences.en: Effectively, we were here firSt.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我们是先到的。

sentences.en: And that sprang from Gavin Menzies' 1421, the year China discovered the world, which basically said these vast treasure fleets had travelled all over the world,
sentences.zh: 这源于加文·孟席斯的《1421：中国发现世界》，该书基本上说这些庞大的宝船队曾航行到世界各地，

sentences.en: as far south as Antarctica to the Americas.
sentences.zh: 南至南极洲，远至美洲。

sentences.en: And two parts of that fleet up the east coast and west coast of Australia in the 1420s.
sentences.zh: 而那支船队的两部分在1420年代沿着澳大利亚的东海岸和西海岸航行。

sentences.en: And the idea is that there are these eunuch admirals.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是基于那些太监提督。

sentences.en: David, fans will be so pleased that you've got in some genital mutilation into this.
sentences.zh: 大卫，粉丝们会很高兴你把生殖器切除术也扯进来了。

sentences.en: Well, I do have a section of my first book called Chinese Salas with No Junk.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的第一本书里确实有一节叫“没有命根子的中国水手”。

sentences.en: And the suggestion has been roundly ridiculed.
sentences.zh: 这个建议遭到了彻底的嘲笑。

sentences.en: Menzies looks at Australian evidence from a chap called Rex Gilroy, who he cites as being some eminent Australian historian.
sentences.zh: 孟席斯参考了一位叫雷克斯·吉尔罗伊的澳大利亚人的证据，他称其为某位杰出的澳大利亚历史学家。

sentences.en: Rex actually wrote for a series of Australian magazines in the 1980s, stories like Why Yowie is a Fair Dinkum, the Yowie being the Australian equivalent of the Bigfoot,
sentences.zh: 雷克斯实际上在1980年代为一系列澳大利亚杂志撰稿，故事包括“为什么澳洲野人是真实存在的”（澳洲野人是澳大利亚版的“大脚怪”），

sentences.en: our own Nessie, about Stonehenge is here.
sentences.zh: 还有关于“我们的尼斯湖水怪”和“巨石阵就在这里”的故事。

sentences.en: And is the sort of guy who wrote stories about UFOs in magazines with topless women on the cover.
sentences.zh: 他就是那种在封面印着上身赤裸女性的杂志上写UFO故事的人。

sentences.en: This is presented by Menzies as a reliable primary source.
sentences.zh: 这被孟席斯当作可靠的一手资料呈现出来。

sentences.en: That's on Holland.
sentences.zh: 那是关于荷兰的。

sentences.en: And it's been labelled as junk history in various Australian exposés of the reliability of those Australian Chinese.
sentences.zh: 在各种关于那些澳大利亚中国论可靠性的揭露中，它被贴上了“垃圾历史”的标签。

sentences.en: So the Chinese didn't come to Australia, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，中国人没有来过澳大利亚。

sentences.en: There's no compelling evidence that the Chinese did come.
sentences.zh: 没有令人信服的证据表明中国人来过。

sentences.en: They would have certainly known once the Macassans started delivering them dried trepang of the existence of the landmass to the south.
sentences.zh: 一旦望加锡人开始向他们运送干海参，他们肯定会知道南部陆地的存在。

sentences.en: But there's no evidence that they themselves came here, no.
sentences.zh: 但没有证据表明他们自己来过这里，没有。

sentences.en: Because they weren't particularly interested in anything that wasn't China.
sentences.zh: 因为他们对中国以外的任何东西都不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: Well, look, the idea is that there is some evidence of these treasure fleets in the 40s.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看，这个想法是说在40年代有这些宝船队的一些证据。

sentences.en: Yeah, they went to Africa, didn't they, and brought back giraffes.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们去了非洲，不是吗，还带回了长颈鹿。

sentences.en: Yeah, and India.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有印度。

sentences.en: But then there was a policy from the 1430s on of effectively isolation and closing themselves off from the world.
sentences.zh: 但从1430年代开始，中国实行了有效的孤立政策，将自己与世界隔绝开来。

sentences.en: So, yeah, no, it's highly speculative at beSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，不，这充其量只是高度推测。

sentences.en: And David, I'm just dredging this up from my memory, so I may have got this wrong.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我只是从记忆中搜寻这些，所以我可能记错了。

sentences.en: Wasn't there quite recently some Arab coins found on a beach that had come from Africa or something?
sentences.zh: 最近是不是在海滩上发现了一些来自非洲的阿拉伯硬币之类的东西？

sentences.en: Look, there are always, yeah, look, there have been some sort of shell-like coins.
sentences.zh: 看，总是有，是的，看，确实有一些类似贝壳的硬币。

sentences.en: There are always bits of old coins and bits of old cannon found on Australian beaches.
sentences.zh: 在澳大利亚海滩上总能发现一些旧硬币和旧大炮的碎片。

sentences.en: Coins, Australia or New South Wales when it was formed was famous for having no currency,
sentences.zh: 硬币，澳大利亚或新南威尔士州在成立时以没有货币而闻名，

sentences.en: a deliberate decision to have no currency where rum becomes the liquid currency of the choice.
sentences.zh: 这是一个故意的决定，没有货币，朗姆酒成了首选的流动货币。

sentences.en: But what you have is you have sailors bringing coins from all over the world that may be, you know, pieces of eight.
sentences.zh: 但你拥有的是水手们从世界各地带来的硬币，可能是，你知道的，西班牙银元。

sentences.en: They may be quite old.
sentences.zh: 它们可能相当古老。

sentences.en: They may have been bought out at some much later time.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是在很久以后才被带出来的。

sentences.en: So, look, before 1606, there's no evidence of any sort of European contact.
sentences.zh: 所以，看，在1606年之前，没有任何欧洲接触的证据。

sentences.en: No compelling evidence of European contact.
sentences.zh: 没有令人信服的欧洲接触证据。

sentences.en: And then what happens in 1606?
sentences.zh: 那么1606年发生了什么？

sentences.en: Why is that such a key date?
sentences.zh: 为什么那是一个如此关键的日期？

sentences.en: Look, there are two things that happened.
sentences.zh: 看，发生了两件事。

sentences.en: The first is that the Dutch East Indies Company has formed in 1602 and they've muscled the Portuguese out of the Spice Islands, bits of Indonesia, to Australia's north.
sentences.zh: 第一是荷兰东印度公司在1602年成立，他们把葡萄牙人从澳大利亚北部的香料群岛和印尼部分地区挤了出去。

sentences.en: And so they are sending ships over to look for spice, send spices back to the Netherlands and around the world.
sentences.zh: 所以他们派船去寻找香料，把香料运回荷兰和世界各地。

sentences.en: And William Jan Cern, the captain of the Doofkin, was sent south from the Spice Islands to look at whether there were new economic opportunities for trade,
sentences.zh: “杜伊夫肯号”的船长威廉·扬茨被从香料群岛派往南方，看看是否有新的贸易经济机会，

sentences.en: for collecting spice or other valuable trade goods.
sentences.zh: 用于收集香料或其他有价值的贸易商品。

sentences.en: And he runs into the Cape York Peninsula in what is now northern Queensland and charts about 300 kilometres of it.
sentences.zh: 他撞上了现在昆士兰北部的约克角半岛，并绘制了约300公里的海岸线。

sentences.en: He calls it Os Papua, thinks it's part of New Guinea.
sentences.zh: 他称之为“新巴布亚”，认为它是新几内亚的一部分。

sentences.en: He names part of New Guinea, New Zealand and sort of sails off in a state of geographical confusion.
sentences.zh: 他命名了新几内亚的一部分，叫“新西兰”，然后在一片地理混乱中航行离开了。

sentences.en: But you do have that Dutch contact in 16...
sentences.zh: 但你确实有16世纪的那次荷兰接触……

sentences.en: So when does Tasman turn up?
sentences.zh: 那么塔斯曼是什么时候出现的？

sentences.en: Tasman turns up in 1642.
sentences.zh: 塔斯曼出现在1642年。

sentences.en: He claims Van Diemen's land.
sentences.zh: 他声称拥有范迪门地。

sentences.en: He's a suck-up.
sentences.zh: 他是个马屁精。

sentences.en: He names it after his boss, Anthony Van Diemen, who's higher up in the Dutch East Indies Company.
sentences.zh: 他以他的老板安东尼·范迪门的名字命名，他在荷兰东印度公司的职位更高。

sentences.en: He goes and paddles around New Zealand and names New Zealand, New Zealand, comes back and names the Australian landmass New Holland.
sentences.zh: 他去新西兰周围划船，命名了新西兰，回来后将澳大利亚大陆命名为“新荷兰”。

sentences.en: That's a great name.
sentences.zh: 那是个好名字。

sentences.en: It's a great shame that it changed.
sentences.zh: 改名真是太可惜了。

sentences.en: The Dutch previously knew Australia as Beach before they called it New Holland.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人在称其为“新荷兰”之前，曾将澳大利亚称为“海滩”。

sentences.en: Beach.
sentences.zh: 海滩。

sentences.en: That's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Full of sand.
sentences.zh: 全是沙子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And when did they discover the Quokka?
sentences.zh: 那么他们是什么时候发现短尾矮袋鼠的呢？

sentences.en: The Quokka?
sentences.zh: 短尾矮袋鼠？

sentences.en: Well, the Quokka lives on Rottnest Island and would have been discovered fairly just off the coast of Perth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，短尾矮袋鼠生活在罗特尼斯岛上，应该是在珀斯海岸附近被发现的。

sentences.en: For those of you who don't know the Quokka, it is not megafauna.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解短尾矮袋鼠的人，它可不是巨型动物。

sentences.en: It is a small, cuddly, smiley kangaroo, much loved by tourists and much loved by starving Dutch sailors who stopped off at the island and ate it.
sentences.zh: 它是一种小巧、可爱、爱笑的袋鼠，深受游客喜爱，也深受那些在岛上停靠并把它吃掉的饥肠辘辘的荷兰水手们的“喜爱”。

sentences.en: So why don't the Dutch...
sentences.zh: 那为什么荷兰人没有……

sentences.en: So, okay, why isn't Australia Dutch?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那为什么澳大利亚不是荷兰的呢？

sentences.en: Okay, so, and also, Dominic, we've got a question here from Eric Mercer.
sentences.zh: 好的，多米尼克，我们这里有一个来自埃里克·默瑟的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: References to New Holland aside, was there any real possibility of the Dutch or indeed the French colonising Australia?
sentences.zh: 撇开“新荷兰”这个称呼不谈，荷兰人或者法国人真的有可能殖民澳大利亚吗？

sentences.en: Or was it always going to be England driven by its loss of the American colonies?
sentences.zh: 还是说，因为失去了美洲殖民地，英国注定会去殖民澳大利亚？

sentences.en: Well, that's the question, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这正是问题的关键，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, why on earth don't people, if they've got their first, or indeed the Portuguese, you know, they're in place.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果他们先到了那里，或者葡萄牙人先到了，毕竟他们当时就在附近，为什么他们没有占领那里呢？

sentences.en: Why on earth are they not all speaking, you know, Dutch or Portuguese in Australia?
sentences.zh: 为什么澳大利亚人说的不是荷兰语或葡萄牙语呢？

sentences.en: Well, look, I mean, as I say, the Portuguese theory of the sort of there in the 1520s on the East Coast is heavily contested.
sentences.zh: 听着，正如我所说，关于葡萄牙人在1520年代到达东海岸的理论，争议非常大。

sentences.en: Those who insist that it is true insist that as a result of the Treaty of Torcedia, I think in 1494, where Spain and Portugal divide the world between themselves and the Pope says,
sentences.zh: 那些坚持这一说法的人认为，这是1494年《托尔德西里亚斯条约》的结果，当时西班牙和葡萄牙瓜分了世界，教皇说：

sentences.en: you have this bit, you have that bit, that the Portuguese were in the wrong place and so were shy about writing their discovery down,
sentences.zh: “这一块归你，那一块归你”，所以葡萄牙人当时在错误的地方，因此对记录下他们的发现感到心虚，

sentences.en: or that all the records burnt in a fire in a library in Lisbon.
sentences.zh: 或者所有的记录都在里斯本的一场图书馆大火中烧毁了。

sentences.en: No evidence of this.
sentences.zh: 但这没有证据。

sentences.en: The Spanish would have colonised Australia.
sentences.zh: 西班牙人本可能会殖民澳大利亚。

sentences.en: And 1606 is an important year because Luis Vaz de Torres sails through the Torres Strait, the body of water that separates Australia from New Guinea,
sentences.zh: 1606年是重要的一年，因为路易斯·瓦斯·德·托雷斯航行穿过了托雷斯海峡，也就是分隔澳大利亚和新几内亚的那片水域，

sentences.en: and actually saw most probably the northernmost tip of Australia thinking it was another island in this sort of sea of treacherous shoals that he desperately wanted to get out of.
sentences.zh: 他很可能看到了澳大利亚的最北端，以为那是这片充满危险浅滩的海域中的另一个岛屿，他当时只想尽快逃离那里。

sentences.en: He didn't stop.
sentences.zh: 他没有停下来。

sentences.en: But if he had, the Spanish would have taken an interest because they were into colonising.
sentences.zh: 但如果他停下来了，西班牙人肯定会感兴趣，因为他们热衷于殖民。

sentences.en: They were interested in spreading Christianity.
sentences.zh: 他们热衷于传播基督教。

sentences.en: They were interested in finding Terra Australis Incognita.
sentences.zh: 他们热衷于寻找“未知的南方大陆”。

sentences.en: And it's lucky for the Brits that they kept on sailing.
sentences.zh: 英国人很幸运，他们（西班牙人）继续航行了。

sentences.en: The Dutch were a mercantile people.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人是一个重商的民族。

sentences.en: And if there was nothing, the East Indies company was a mercantile company.
sentences.zh: 如果那里什么都没有，东印度公司就是一家商业公司。

sentences.en: It was sort of a projection of Dutch power, but it operated independently of the government.
sentences.zh: 它算是荷兰势力的一种延伸，但独立于政府运作。

sentences.en: And it was only interested in setting up trading posts where there was something to buy or sell.
sentences.zh: 它只对在有买卖可做的地方建立贸易站感兴趣。

sentences.en: And they decided that the bits of Australia that they stopped off at had lots of sand, which there wasn't a great market for.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他们停靠的澳大利亚部分全是沙子，而沙子没什么大市场。

sentences.en: They did stop off.
sentences.zh: 他们确实停靠过。

sentences.en: They hit the West Australian coast in 1616, a chap called Dirk Hartog, who nails a pewter plate to a post, which basically says Dirk Hartog was here,
sentences.zh: 1616年，一个叫德克·哈托格的人抵达了西澳大利亚海岸，他在柱子上钉了一块锡盘，上面写着德克·哈托格到此一游，

sentences.en: which was the Dutch way of sort of saying we're here.
sentences.zh: 这就是荷兰人宣告“我们在这儿”的方式。

sentences.en: The French, when they came, left bottles lying around bits of the Australian coast with messages in them.
sentences.zh: 法国人来的时候，会在澳大利亚海岸边留下装有信息的瓶子。

sentences.en: You know, I, Marion de Frasnay, was here.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是“我，马里昂·杜弗雷纳，到此一游”。

sentences.en: The French come to and sail up the coast of Western Australia in 1687.
sentences.zh: 法国人在1687年航行到了西澳大利亚海岸。

sentences.en: A bloke called Abraham de Quisney-Guiton cites the Swan River, but keeps on sailing for the Spice Islands to the north.
sentences.zh: 一个叫亚伯拉罕·德·基斯内-吉顿的人发现了天鹅河，但为了去北方的香料群岛，他继续航行了。

sentences.en: The French weren't terribly interested in colonisation at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时法国人对殖民并不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: They were interested in trade and sort of scientific discovery.
sentences.zh: 他们对贸易和科学发现更感兴趣。

sentences.en: So, the Spanish would have taken a more active interest if they'd stopped off.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果西班牙人停下来，他们会更积极地进行殖民。

sentences.en: French and Dutch, not so much.
sentences.zh: 法国人和荷兰人则没那么大兴趣。

sentences.en: And even the Brits, when Cook arrives in 1770, Joseph Banks, you know, the scientific go-to guy aboard the Endeavour.
sentences.zh: 即使是英国人，当库克在1770年到达时，约瑟夫·班克斯，也就是“奋进号”上的科学顾问，

sentences.en: He's a botanist who gives the name BotaniSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位植物学家，他给植物学家命名。

sentences.en: He's a botanist who is the inspiration for Mr. Spock in Star Trek.
sentences.zh: 他是一位植物学家，也是《星际迷航》中史波克先生的灵感来源。

sentences.en: He, he, and James Cook was the inspiration for James Kirk.
sentences.zh: 他，他，而詹姆斯·库克是詹姆斯·柯克的灵感来源。

sentences.en: Star Trek was modelled on the Endeavour voyage.
sentences.zh: 《星际迷航》是以“奋进号”的航行为蓝本的。

sentences.en: But Banks says the country reminded him of the back of a lean cow and his sort of scathing of its suitability for settlement.
sentences.zh: 但班克斯说，这片土地让他想起了瘦牛的背，他对这里是否适合定居评价很刻薄。

sentences.en: Until 1878, when he has a change of heart, the American War of Independence, Britain's desperately looking for somewhere new to dump its convicts.
sentences.zh: 直到1778年，他改变了主意，当时美国独立战争爆发，英国急于寻找新的地方来安置囚犯。

sentences.en: And Banks says, well, this place wasn't so bad.
sentences.zh: 班克斯说，嗯，这个地方其实还不错。

sentences.en: So, but you still have a period of 10 years where the Brits look at the idea of convict settlements in East Africa, the West Indies.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那之后的10年里，英国人考虑过在东非、西印度群岛建立囚犯定居点。

sentences.en: They again try to send some convicts to the Americas, the Mosquito CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 他们再次尝试把一些囚犯送到美洲，送到蚊子海岸。

sentences.en: Next, New South Wales was very much an afterthought and it appealed to the Brits, not so much because of anything that Cook or Banks said, but it was so geographically isolated.
sentences.zh: 接下来，新南威尔士州很大程度上是一个事后补救措施，它吸引英国人并不是因为库克或班克斯说了什么，而是因为它地理位置太偏僻了。

sentences.en: There was no, no other Western settlement about.
sentences.zh: 周围没有其他西方定居点。

sentences.en: And when you sent your convicts to America, they kept on popping on boats and coming home.
sentences.zh: 当你把囚犯送到美国时，他们总是跳上船跑回家。

sentences.en: The idea was that if you dumped convicts in Botany Bay, which rapidly moved to Sydney, they wouldn't be able to get back.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，如果你把囚犯扔在植物湾（后来很快转移到了悉尼），他们就回不来了。

sentences.en: And so that ended up being.
sentences.zh: 结果就是这样。

sentences.en: Except we said Mackwich.
sentences.zh: 除了我们说的麦克威奇。

sentences.en: Mackwich does come back.
sentences.zh: 麦克威奇确实回来了。

sentences.en: Well, look, the irony is that the first convicts actually escaped within a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，讽刺的是，第一批囚犯在几周内就逃跑了。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: French vessels.
sentences.zh: 法国船只。

sentences.en: Peter Paris, a French waiter, hitched a ride off.
